correctness.rationale: For n=pq (p<q distinct primes), checking all four positive divisors reduces exactly, by CRT and Fermat, to q|p^(p−1)−1 and p|q^(q−1)−1. Bang–Zsigmondy for (p,1,h=p−1) has no exceptional case for p≥5, so a primitive q has ord_q(p)=p−1, p−1|(q−1), q>p; Fermat supplies the second condition. Taking one q per p gives distinct products because p is always the smaller factor; pq<p^p. For Y=floor(log X/loglog X), Y log Y<log X and the prime number theorem yield S₂(X)≥π(Y)−2 and stated liminf at least one. Two-prime Korselt divisibility excludes every constructed n from ordinary Carmichael numbers. Independent code checked all 5,047 distinct semiprimes <=20,000 (25 satisfying) by the original and reduced criteria and several order witnesses. The finite checks do not certify Zsigmondy, the PNT, or the infinite conclusion.
